statement: Apples cost 3 cents each. Pia has 20 cents. What is the largest number of apples she can buy?

choices.misconception: I rounded up, but 7 apples cost 21 cents, which is more than Pia has.
I took 3 away from 20 only once instead of seeing how many 3s fit into 20.
I added the 3 cents and the 20 cents together.
I multiplied 3 by 20 instead of seeing how many 3s fit into 20.

hints: Count up in 3s and stop before you pass 20.
Each apple adds 3 cents to the cost. Count the cost in steps of 3 until the next step would cost more than Pia has. Money left over cannot buy a whole apple.
3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 cents buys 6 apples. A seventh apple would make the cost 21 cents.

solutions.reliable: Count the cost in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. Six apples cost 18 cents and leave 2 cents, which is not enough for another apple. Seven apples would cost 21 cents, more than 20. So Pia can buy 6 apples. The idea to keep: when money runs short, the leftover does not buy one more.

whyOnTest: Buying as many as you can afford checks whether a child stops at the right step instead of rounding up.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
